subject: Pay-as-you-go liquidity bucket & advance-remit proposal (VAT split)
messages:
From: Samir Kulkarni <samir@ledgercloud.com>

Cc: procurement@ledgercloud.com
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Request: pay-as-you-go bucket + VAT handling

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile and the model routing suggestions. Procurement asked me to follow up on billing because we have a few constraints:

- We prefer a pay-as-you-go ‘bucket’ that draws down as we run inference (not a large committed annual prepay).
- For cashflow predictability we’d accept a small advance deposit that gets consumed against usage, with top-ups at predefined thresholds.
- Our finance team is in the EU; we need clarity on VAT handling (are you charging VAT on invoices or do we self-account?).
- Finally, we need a short-term credit cap (one month) while we finalize internal approvals — ideally a rolling $50k buffer.

Can you send a proposed structure and example schedule (monthly forecast vs actual consumption) and any required tax artifacts? Procurement would like to move quickly if pricing holds.

Thanks,
Samir
Procurement Manager, LedgerCloud

Attachment: forecast_sample.csv (referenced)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Samir Kulkarni <samir@ledgercloud.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 12:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: pay-as-you-go bucket + VAT handling

Hi Samir — great to hear. Below is a compact proposal that balances your preference for usage-based billing with Redwood’s need to manage risk and VAT compliance. I’m copying Finance and Sales Ops to confirm operational feasibility.

Proposal (high level):
1) Liquidity bucket (pay-as-you-go):
   - LedgerCloud prepays an initial liquidity bucket equivalent to 10% of a 12-month forecast (min $10k). That deposit is held as credit and consumed per token/embedding usage.
   - If remaining balance falls below 30% of the initial deposit, automatic top-up to bring it back to 60% (charge to the card/PO on file). Top-up triggers can be disabled with a signed PO for manual top-ups.

2) Advance-remit + rolling buffer:
   - Temporary rolling credit lane up to $50k while procurement completes approvals. This is a time-bound facility (30 days) and requires a signed short-form schedule and the initial 10% deposit.
   - If usage exceeds the $50k buffer within 30 days, service will continue for an additional 72 hours to allow remediation; after 72 hours we’ll reduce concurrency/throughput until either top-up or PO arrives.

3) Invoice rhythm and net terms:
   - Monthly invoice covering net consumption minus bucket credits. Default terms: NET30.
   - Alternate: NET45 for customers with >$250k ARR or a 1.5% finance fee on outstanding balance if requesting NET45 for smaller accounts.

4) VAT handling (EU):
   - Redwood will charge VAT on invoices shipped to EU-registered legal entities where local VAT is applicable.
   - If LedgerCloud provides a valid EU VAT registration certificate and invoicing is to a B2B legal entity with reverse-charge permitted, we will zero-rate the VAT and include the VAT registration reference on invoices; LedgerCloud will self-account per local regulations.
   - Please attach your VAT certificate (example filename: ledgercloud_vat_certificate.pdf).

5) Attachments & next steps:
   - Attached: redwood_proposed_payment_schedule.xlsx (example drawdown & top-up cadence).
   - If acceptable, we’ll issue a short-form order schedule and DocuSign (or accept a PO + VAT cert).

Operational notes: Grace — will Sales Ops need any extra steps to enable the auto-top-up? Sergio — Finance: do we need additional credit paperwork for a 30-day $50k rolling buffer? Lauren — legal: short-form signature ok?

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk the procurement team through the example schedule.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_proposed_payment_schedule.xlsx
